assertions.name: C1_tau_reproduces_the_DG_WORKED_figure_eight_value
assertions.source: |tau(4_1)| = sqrt(3)/2 to 0.0. This validates the implementation being consumed — the module records that THREE 1-loop implementations existed in this repo and disagreed, so consuming one without this check would be unsafe

assertions.name: C3_the_retriangulator_REALLY_perturbs_the_triangulation
assertions.source: every knot shows >1 distinct polarization datum, so the invariance test below is not vacuous — an invariance check passes trivially when nothing was varied

assertions.name: the_RAW_POLARIZATION_datum_is_NOT_a_manifold_invariant
assertions.source: one manifold, 30 retriangulations: 6_2 gives 7 distinct values, 5_2 7, 4_1 3. The node count IS a manifold invariant, so a construction reading the matrix entries directly cannot equal it without a separate triangulation-invariance argument

assertions.name: C2_tau_IS_triangulation_invariant
assertions.source: spread < 1e-30 over retriangulations of 4_1 and 6_2, while C3 confirms the triangulation genuinely changed. So triangulation-invariant functionals of the NZ datum EXIST

assertions.name: tau_SEPARATES_all_five_knots_the_SNF_could_not
assertions.source: all 10 pairwise gaps exceed 1e-30; the smallest is 0.555151. The SNF gave these five knots ONE value; a triangulation-invariant functional of the same datum gives five

assertions.name: NO_tau_to_C_map_is_proposed_and_none_can_be_TESTED_here
assertions.source: certified connection counts exist for exactly 3 knots (4_1, 5_2, 3_1 — the snappy wheel's Magma fixtures; the ptolemy DB is firewalled), and tau is UNDEFINED on 3_1 because it is not hyperbolic. That leaves TWO usable (tau, C) points, which any two-parameter family fits exactly. A map fitted here would be unfalsifiable by construction, so none is offered

assertions.name: CONSEQUENCE_the_dictionary_is_LOCATED_not_excluded
assertions.source: it must be strictly finer than the Smith normal form (part 1) and triangulation-invariant (this part). That class is non-empty — tau is in it — so D1-b is narrowed to a well-posed search, not refuted. What is missing to PROSECUTE that search is data: more certified connection counts, i.e. the ptolemy database or magma

description: D1-b (qou-q9ih) part 2, closing the side part 1 left open. Part 1: the SNF of the NZ gluing matrix is a function of N alone, so the dictionary must be polarization-dependent. Here: the raw polarization-dependent datum is NOT a manifold invariant -- 30 retriangulations of 6_2 give ~a dozen distinct values of (N, SNF(P), det P, rank P) for P = A_edge.B_edge^T -- the exact count is STOCHASTIC, randomize() walks a random move sequence and successive runs gave 9 and 11, so read this run's figures from polarization_variance_under_retriangulation rather than quoting one; the assertion tests only that it moves. Together a pincer: the basis-independent invariant is too coarse, the raw polarization datum too fine, and the node count is a manifold invariant. CONSTRUCTIVE half: the class of triangulation-invariant NZ functionals is non-empty and the corpus holds a verified member -- the Dimofte-Garoufalidis 1-loop invariant tau (one_loop_torsion.py), measured here as triangulation-invariant to 1e-30 and separating all five N=5 knots the SNF collided. So D1-b's dictionary is LOCATED, not excluded. NO tau->C map is proposed: certified C exists for only three knots and tau is undefined on the non-hyperbolic 3_1, leaving TWO usable points, which any two-parameter family fits exactly -- such a proposal would be unfalsifiable in this corpus by construction. mpmath at 40 dps throughout; no float64. Scope-(a); nothing wired; no fit.

scope.shows: the raw polarization-dependent NZ datum is not a manifold invariant; together with part 1's SNF degeneracy this brackets the dictionary between too-coarse and too-fine
scope.constructive: the bracketed class is non-empty; the DG 1-loop tau is triangulation-invariant and separates the five N=5 knots the SNF collided
scope.does_NOT_show: that tau, or any triangulation-invariant functional, PRODUCES the node count. tau is a complex number, not an integer count; separating is not counting
scope.why_no_map_is_offered: only two usable (tau, C) points exist in this corpus (3_1 is non-hyperbolic so tau is undefined there), and any two-parameter family fits two points exactly
scope.what_would_unblock: more certified connection counts — the ptolemy database (firewalled) or magma
scope.arithmetic: mpmath at 40 dps for tau; exact integers for the polarization datum; no float64, no float() outside mp.nstr rendering
